records.name: Annie Andrews
records.what: Campaigned on a two-year data-center moratorium and local control; WSOC-TV reported the platform in its coverage of her win over Darline Graham.

records.name: Angie Nixon
records.what: Campaigning in Gainesville alongside Sen. Bernie Sanders, said she supports restrictions on AI data centers.

records.name: Larry Marker
records.what: Asked by The Eastern New Mexico News how the federal government should regulate data centers, answered that local city or county ordinances should address where they go: “Each county can and should determine if they want data centers or not.”

records.name: Ben Ray Luján
records.what: In a KVIA voter-guide questionnaire, said data centers “should not use our drinking water or water used for agricultural purposes” and “should also be required to generate their own power rather than strain the grid,” adding that “New Mexicans should not pay a penny more for their electricity.” He cited bipartisan legislation he wrote aimed at stopping water waste and protecting community drinking water.

records.name: Angie Nixon
records.what: On a moratorium: “I think there needs to be a moratorium until more research is done.” She said she is not opposed to AI or technological innovation but wants tougher guardrails around privacy, employment and data-center construction, and quipped that “if people want to build a data center, they should put it on Mar-a-Lago.”

records.name: Ashley Moody
records.what: Cosponsored Sen. Jon Husted’s Ratepayer Protection Act, directing state utility regulators and unregulated utilities to consider rules making data centers pay the full added cost of new generation, transmission or distribution needed to serve them, post financial guarantees before upgrades begin, and cover costs if they end power contracts early. “Floridians should not be left to foot the bill.” After Senate Democrats blocked it: “While Democrats continue to play politics over the issue, I’ll keep fighting to get this common-sense legislation passed.”

records.name: Suhas Subramanyam
records.what: At a Brookings Institution event called the community-by-community approach to data center siting "short-term profit-driven, sometimes it's a little predatory, and it's not working" and said he wants "a national strategy that puts communities first"; also called for transparency in development agreements, which often include nondisclosure agreements signed by officials, and on actual power and water use.

records.name: Bert Mizusawa
records.what: In a Charlottesville Tomorrow / VPM candidate Q&A, backed “the ability of local communities, who will bear the costs, to veto having data centers” rather than having them “forced on them by Richmond or Washington, DC,” said “Data centers can and should be located in remote areas,” and called for rapid deployment of newer nuclear reactors. He stated no position on ratepayer costs, water use or data-center tax breaks.

records.name: Chris Pappas
records.what: Statement on the vote: “data centers and other large-load consumers shouldn’t be given a free pass to hike electric rates” and “they should pay their own way.” He also said the bill would “put the decision of whether data center construction can move forward in the hands of Granite Staters.”

records.name: Greg Casar
records.what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), added 09/17/2026.

records.name: Chris Pappas
records.what: Voted for H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, which directs state utility regulators to consider requiring 100 MW-plus large-load customers to cover the full added cost of generation, transmission and distribution upgrades they need. The House passed it 417-3.

records.name: Peggy Flanagan
records.what: A Forum News Service report on the candidates' positions said she emphasises Minnesotans not paying Big Tech's costs and opposes major tax breaks for Big Tech, and quoted her: “Communities get to call the shots.” It said she thinks NDA use for data centers should be banned, that they should be built with union labor and that they should meet Minnesota's environmental standards. records.name: Michele Tafoya
records.what: Said in a statement reported by Forum News Service that Minnesota should welcome new economic growth but projects “have to work for the communities where they're being built”; that residents, farmers and businesses deserve a real say and “certainly shouldn't be left paying the bill”; and that developers must be upfront about what they need, what incentives they receive and how they will cover the costs their projects create. records.what: At the Ohio Energy Affordability Summit announced he will introduce legislation imposing a federal tax equal to 100% of any state or local tax incentive given to a data center, saying "I don't want a single taxpayer dollar going to support these data centers."

records.name: James C. Justice
records.what: At the West Virginia Chamber of Commerce annual meeting, urged attendees not to fear data centers but said companies must be responsible neighbors: 'If you're going to come to West Virginia and you're going to do something in West Virginia, you need to be taking care of everybody. The environment, the water, the electricity bills, the noise. You've got to take care of everybody, and there's a way to do it.'

records.name: Brad Finstad
records.what: Said data centers "can play an important role in our economic future and national security, but the decision...should be made by the people and local leaders who know their communities best, not handed down by Washington"; emphasized need for corporate transparency.

records.name: Tom Emmer
records.what: MinnPost reported Emmer “immediately embraced” Trump’s message of support for data centers. In a post on X he said Trump was “absolutely spot on” and that “Communist China and our adversaries would love it if the United States was asleep at the wheel and stopped innovating and developing AI and emerging tech.”

records.name: Maggie Goodlander
records.what: Debate (WMUR, via InDepthNH): said some communities are seeing more than 200% increases in energy prices because of data centers; people and communities 'have got to have the ultimate say in whether a data center comes into their community'; reporter paraphrases her as calling for transparency and accountability and for the corporations to pay rather than taxpayers.

records.name: Paige Beauchemin
records.what: Debate (WMUR, via InDepthNH): reporter says she supports stopping the construction of any data centers until legislation can be introduced to regulate the issue; quoted: 'Those kinds of regulations need to ensure that environmental impact studies initially and ongoing, they need to ensure that utility costs are paid for by the companies and not from the other folks, and we also need to make sure that the local folks have their own local control.'

records.name: Tommy Tuberville
records.what: Op-ed "My game plan for data centers": "Local communities will decide whether a data center is right for them"; data centers go in "Alabama's highest property-tax bracket" with no abatements; companies must "pay the total cost of the transmission lines, substations and water systems" they need; pledges to freeze Alabama Power rates through 2029 and beyond.

records.name: Katie Boyd Britt
records.what: Defended the Trump administration's nonbinding Ratepayer Protection Pledge as "an outstanding first step to protecting Alabamians and ratepayers," and said communities should weigh "the amount of power that's taken" against tax revenue.

records.name: Pete Ricketts
records.what: At the Nebraska State Fair U.S. Senate debate said "when it comes to data centers, local control is the name of the game," that communities "should negotiate first" and are "in the driver's seat," and should insist "you shouldn't impact my power rates. You should conserve water - closed-loop systems," then ask for more in property taxes.

records.name: Bruce Westerman
records.what: Town hall: 'We are in a Cold War with China on developing AI technology'; 'we have to develop AI. To develop AI, you have to have data centers'; on water, 'I don't think is as big an issue as what some people make it out to be'; said data center companies 'are willing to pay for that new generating equipment' and transmission, and that communities should define water and electrical requirements and hold the companies accountable.

records.name: Lauren Boebert
records.what: Asked by a MeidasTouch reporter about Trump saying data center opponents are 'backwards and poor,' said 'The president says a lot of things. Sometimes, it's really funny... Anyway, I fought for data centers to have local control' and 'I want people to have local control. That's what I fought for.'

records.name: Steve Scalise
records.what: Told Fox Business: 'We are investigating whether China is behind a lot of this misinformation, false information against data centers,' and said Republicans are 'finding some things,' including Beijing-controlled social media bots.

records.name: Lily Tang Williams
records.what: GOP debate (WMUR, via InDepthNH): 'I would say no government perks, credits and taxpayer dollars should be involved. If a private company wants to come here, build data centers, then they need to respect our local control and address our concerns of environmental impact and electricity costs.'

records.name: Tim Burchett
records.what: Responded to Trump's warning that communities rejecting data centers risk becoming 'backwards and poor' by saying 'I guess I'm backwards and poor.' Called for more local control and suggested putting data centers in military installations.

records.name: John Fetterman
records.what: Posted on X, as quoted by the Philadelphia Inquirer, that he agreed with President Trump's defense of data centers: "There's nothing more damaging to a Democrat than agreeing with Trump AND data centers — but what's right is right," and "We must win the war for AI supremacy over China."

records.name: John Thune
records.what: Told KELOLAND that data centers 'need to be self-sufficient. They ought to be able to take care of their own utilities, their own power, and that ought to be a given any place they go in the country. But they shouldn't be going places where there isn't support for them at the local level.'

records.name: Stephanie Bice
records.what: Statement responding to President's comments on data centers: 'it is vital that local communities have a voice in the decisions on proposed data centers'; applauded Oklahoma legislature for passing ratepayer protection and groundwater laws

records.name: Roy Cooper
records.what: Said in a local interview that “we need to make sure data centers pay for their own power” and should be encouraged to build their own energy sources, framing it as part of his “make stuff cost less” campaign. Fox News described this as a shift from his time as governor, when he applauded data center growth, and noted that the bulk of the state's tax breaks already existed when he took office in 2017.

records.name: Raphael G. Warnock
records.what: Speaking in Guyton near OpenAI's proposed Effingham County site, called for a data center pause in Georgia — "In the absence of Congress not getting its act together and putting some common-sense guardrails in place, local communities and states find themselves in a race to the bottom" — with conditions: no increase in residents' water or electric bills, no water/air/noise/light pollution, no NDAs, no "sweetheart tax giveaways"; "This is not OpenAI County — this is Effingham County."

records.name: Michael Rulli
records.what: On Fox Business's Mornings with Maria, said 'Most of my constituents do not like data centers. They don't want them.' Told constituents to learn 'in front of the meter' (you pay) vs 'behind the meter' (the company pays) and whether the water system is self-contained, said data centers 'shouldn't put them on waste lands, brown fields' and 'Keep them out of the corn fields. Keep them out of the neighborhoods. We need to do better.' Also said 'The CCP has infiltrated Ohio with propaganda against this.' Did not state a position on the OpenAI/Nvidia project by name.

records.name: Roy Cooper
records.what: Campaign position, via a spokesperson: “Data centers must pay for all of the energy they use without passing on any of their costs to consumers.” Spectrum News reported that both he and his opponent support letting local communities block data centers and that neither has backed a federal moratorium. It also noted numerous data centers were built while he was governor; his campaign said the tax breaks were signed into law in 2006 and expanded in 2015, before his term.

records.name: Michael Whatley
records.what: A campaign spokesman told Spectrum News his standard is that “data centers pay their own way, families pay nothing, and communities decide”, with Big Tech covering the grid upgrades it needs and no costs shifted onto residential ratepayers. In the same podcast interview where he called opposition “ginned up”, he said there must be no disparate impact on a community's water, traffic or electricity. Spectrum reported that both he and his opponent support letting communities block data centers and that neither backed a federal moratorium.

records.name: Kweisi Mfume
records.what: Added as a cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), on 08/27/2026.

records.name: Josh Brecheen
records.what: Town hall, McAlester: said operators 'have to make sure that they are not driving up people's electricity costs'; 'Congress is not gonna create the regulatory environment. What we can do is make sure people have information about the data centers.' Co-sponsors HR9019 requiring the Energy Secretary to report to Congress on data center electricity and water use.

records.name: Ted Cruz
records.what: On NewsNation's 'Katie Pavlich Tonight', Cruz said 'the concerns being raised about data centers are real and reasonable' and suggested developers offer residents direct payments or tell them 'your electricity bill is zero for the rest of your life. We will pay your electric bill—forever.'

records.name: Mike Rogers
records.what: Announced he was calling for a one-year moratorium on new data center construction in Michigan, The Hill reported.

records.name: Gabe Vasquez
records.what: Per his Aug 25 release, was 'the only statewide or federal official' to publicly call for an end to the Socorro County data center proposal; the developer pulled out and commissioners unanimously approved a one-year moratorium.

records.name: Gabe Vasquez
records.what: Announced support for the FAIR Data Act (H.R. 9655), which would force large corporate electricity users to pay their own way so residential customers and small businesses do not cover data center costs.

records.name: John Fetterman
records.what: Posted on X, as quoted by TribLive: "AI supremacy and energy dominance underpins our national security" and "I reject the political pandering and hyperbole over data centers," adding "America must lead in the development of AI, otherwise we live under China's rules."

records.name: John Barrasso
records.what: On a proposal to site data centers on public lands, told Cowboy State Daily: 'Development of federal land, including the construction of new data centers, deserves meaningful input from state and local governments and the public. The people of Wyoming expect to have their voices heard.'

records.name: Ken Paxton
records.what: Released a four-point plan: back legislation barring Chinese technology from powering data centers and holding developers criminally liable where their infrastructure powers AI chatbots that endanger children; co-sponsor Sen. Tom Cotton's DATA Act, which would exempt new off-grid electricity providers from certain federal regulations; and advocate for Gov. Abbott's state-level data center plan.

records.name: Ken Paxton
records.what: The Texas Tribune reported his plan also champions Abbott's push to repeal the industry's sales-tax exemptions and backs a ban on AI data centers in rural Texas. It noted that as a state senator in 2013 he voted for the data center sales-tax exemption; that Hood County's February request for an attorney general opinion on whether it could impose a data center moratorium was still undecided six months later; and that NOTUS reported his political operation had taken nearly $450,000 from data-center-affiliated donors.

records.name: Paul LePage
records.what: Said 'I'm a big, big fan of data centers... I think they're going to create jobs. I think we can solve our energy problems' at a former mill site in Lincoln; downplayed water and power concerns. His campaign said Friday he supports 'sensible regulation,' including guarantees of adequate water supply, local community buy-in and no rate hikes for consumers.

records.name: Matthew Dunlap
records.what: Campaign warned 'if we don't approach these projects deliberately they will jack up energy prices'; favors developing benchmarks and standards for worker benefits, ratepayer impact, and community benefits

records.name: Melanie Stansbury
records.what: Formal letter to five NM state officials demanding written answers on Project Jupiter's water use, water rights, permits, and Rio Grande Compact compliance; called it 'an important test case for how New Mexico evaluates major industrial water users'

records.name: Bill Cassidy
records.what: Quoted praising Meta's Richland Parish data center: 'Economic growth increases the tax base and sales tax revenue' and 'Teacher bonuses there are up to $50,000 this year.'

records.name: Jon Husted
records.what: Said in February that data centers should be “producing their own electricity so that it doesn't hit ratepayers” and recycling the water in their systems. A leaked National Republican Senatorial Committee memo called data centers “the anchor hanging around Husted's neck.”

records.name: Katie Boyd Britt
records.what: Said data center decisions "need to be made on a local level," that communities that reject a proposal "shouldn't be forced" to proceed, and that neither "a data center on every corner" nor "a full moratorium" is the right avenue; backs the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge.

records.name: John Thune
records.what: In an August 2026 South Dakota appearance, Thune called energy permitting reform a rare bipartisan opportunity, citing utilities' rapidly growing demand 'including that associated with data centers'; he framed faster permitting as the way to add generation and transmission.
records.source_name: KOTA Territory TV / South Dakota Searchlight

records.name: Mike Rogers
records.what: Reversed his position and backed a statewide moratorium days after The Lever reported that he holds between $1.7 million and $2.6 million in companies that stand to benefit from tech-friendly policies and faster permitting for AI development. His campaign did not say whether he was considering divesting.

records.name: Tom Barrett
records.what: Introduced H.R. 10119, the Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (prohibits federal agencies from overriding local land-use, zoning, siting or permitting authority related to data centers and from leveraging federal funds to force local governments to give up that authority) and H.R. 10118, the No Data Center NDAs Act (prohibits members of Congress from signing NDAs about data centers, including locations or expected water and energy use). "They deserve to know all the facts and have the final say over any proposed project." His release says that in the Michigan House he voted against legislation giving data center construction and equipment tax breaks.

records.name: Susan M. Collins
records.what: Told the Bangor Daily News data-center projects should be handled case by case, favoring former mill sites because "there is usually hydropower right there," while saying "I do share the concern of data centers gobbling up too much energy and putting stress on the cost of energy."

records.name: Steven Horsford
records.what: At a town hall on AI and automation with Khanna, advocated advance notice and training for workers and collective bargaining as accountability tools (about worker automation, not data centers).

records.name: Darline Graham
records.what: In the South Carolina GOP Senate debate said: "Obviously, I just said I'm for data centers, but I also said that there needs to be community involvement, community guidelines, community guardrails."

records.name: Mike Lawler
records.what: On Fox Business's Mornings with Maria, said of Hochul's data center pause: 'What she is saying is, don't come here. Go do your business elsewhere, which is why New York State leads the nation in out-migration.' Also said New York has 'the highest tax burden and the worst business climate'.

records.name: Jen Kiggans
records.what: Told The Daily Signal: “They have data centers under the ocean floor. We can’t ban all data centers,” adding there is a “commonsense conversation to be had” on their use of energy, water and other local resources, that the debate has so far been left to Virginia’s Legislature, and that she has “enjoyed watching the Democrats fight with each other about the issue.”

records.name: Dina Titus
records.what: Asked Gov. Lombardo to refrain from approving data center tax abatements for projects on BLM land until the Legislature reconvenes to reconsider; the governor's reply did not commit to halting abatements.

records.name: Pat Fallon
records.what: Told CBS News Texas: 'I think it was a thoughtful, good step that the governor put in place. He was listening to his constituents... They share those concerns, as I do.' Referring to Abbott's data center directives, which CBS describes as including a pause.

records.name: JoAnna Mendoza
records.what: Said: 'No data centers in the desert... Not right now, not in our district, not in our state.' Also said 'We can't have data centers near residential areas,' citing ASU research that air-cooled data centers emit heat 'anywhere between two to four degrees more,' and warned energy bills would go up.

records.name: Andrea Salinas
records.what: Introduced Data Center Community Reinvestment Act establishing 1-cent-per-kWh excise tax on data center electricity consumption (>1 MW capacity), directing $1.76B/year to Land and Water Conservation Fund, Housing Trust Fund, Superfund, Highway Trust Fund, and Energy Technology Trust Fund

records.name: Gabe Vasquez
records.what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9825, the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026 (sponsor Rep. Underwood), whose official title is to require data center operators to submit reports on data center energy and water use; added as a cosponsor 08/13/2026.

records.name: Dan Sullivan
records.what: Asked in Kodiak about a rumored Navy data center at the Naval Special Warfare detachment on Spruce Cape, said "I had never heard of that issue until last week," "I think it's a rumor," and "if it's true, I think it's a bad idea and I will work to stop it."

records.name: Amy Klobuchar
records.what: In a KFGO interview during her run for governor said data centers "cause people's rates to go up, they have hurt the environment, and that just can't keep happening," criticized non-disclosure agreements keeping projects "in the dark," and called for local control over siting decisions.

records.name: Adrian Smith
records.what: At Nebraska energy summit: 'The efficiencies that can be achieved already with AI, it's amazing... We should not stand in the way. We should celebrate how much better lives can be with more economic efficiency out there that can be a result of AI.' Article reports the delegation advocated for data centers while a dozen-plus counties weighed moratoriums, and that members said AI should have rules without specifics.

records.name: Rand Paul
records.what: During a visit to Fort Knox, on data center siting: 'I don't think the federal government should regulate where data centers are placed or built, nor do I think the governor should. Each county should make this decision at the most local level.' He added that counties with a large tax base might not want one while poorer counties might.

records.name: Bill Hagerty
records.what: During a Knoxville visit, asked about East Tennessee local governments' 12-month data-center moratoriums, Hagerty said 'we made it very clear to the data centers that they're going to have to make the investment, not only in our capacity but in our grid,' and that tech companies must ensure consumers are not 'bearing the burden' of the facilities.

records.name: Luke Bronin
records.what: Victory speech called for 'sensible artificial intelligence regulation'; published platform says 'We need guardrails' against algorithmic addiction of kids and 'machines that act without human input or oversight'. The article records no data-center position.

records.name: Paul Tonko
records.what: Said at an Albany roundtable that data centers like the one proposed for the Kenwood site in South Albany "should be built in communities that want them", and that "we have to provide for those safety nets and the guardrails for both AI and data centers."

records.name: Sherrod Brown
records.what: Attacked Husted's record of supporting tax breaks for data-center developers in two July ads and, in a third, promised to make data centers pay the full cost of their electricity use. He called for ending the data center tax breaks and said local communities should decide whether data centers are built. He did not back a halt to construction.

records.name: Jon Husted
records.what: The Ohio Capital Journal reported he introduced the bill one day after an ad from his opponent on data centers was released, that as lieutenant governor he backed tens of millions of dollars in tax breaks for data center projects, and that he has otherwise called data centers a “local issue” the federal government should stay out of.

records.name: Ron Wyden
records.what: As Finance Committee ranking member released a white paper proposing to remove existing tax investment incentives as applied to data centers and create a Data Center Public Investment excise tax, with revenue for workers displaced by AI; said communities "are rightfully questioning whether the rapid buildout of data centers across the nation will benefit them, as local disruptions rise."

records.name: Ro Khanna
records.what: Introduced the Data Center Bill of Rights resolution: communities may ban data centers in residential areas and within 2,500 feet of homes, schools, childcare, hospitals or nursing homes; may reject a project through a transparent community process; county and municipal authority to prohibit or regulate is preserved against state preemption; and every data center must use clean, reliable energy under strict noise and air limits. It is a resolution, so it does not itself change law.

records.name: Ace Parsi
records.what: Said at a virtual 'Candidates Against Transmission Lines' news conference: 'People don't feel like they're listened to or represented, because if nobody wants these, how did this go through such an overwhelming majority in the House and Senate.' Said the architects behind the data-center build-out have been withholding information. (HB 2014 repeal was called for by another candidate, Vince George.)

records.name: Chuck Gray
records.what: At a Sheridan forum said: 'I'm the only candidate on stage that has been talking about these data AI data centers and expressed my opposition to these AI data centers.' Reporter: only Gray has indicated a desire to ban them at the federal level.

records.name: Chuck Gray
records.what: Same article: Rasner said Gray voted in 2021 for data-center tax breaks; the article confirms Gray voted to keep the tax exemption, and that his signature is on the business registration approval for Terra Crypto, tied by a 2024 order to MineOne, which Gray denied wrongdoing over.

records.name: Eugene Vindman
records.what: Introduced the Smart Data Center Policy Act, directing the Department of Commerce to study the costs, benefits and possible federal incentives for siting data centers in industrial zones, rail and airport hubs and military installations rather than near homes and green space, with findings due to Congress in 180 days. Vindman: “We need to ensure data centers pay their fair share and are built in places that make sense — not next to neighborhoods, schools, or our public lands.”

records.name: Amy Klobuchar
records.what: Through spokesman Darwin Forsyth, said she "supports robust environmental standards for any proposed data centers as well as greater transparency and local control over decisions to build," called Minnesota's 2025 law requiring data centers to pay the full cost of their energy use "a good start," and said her focus would be protecting Minnesotans' energy bills and water; she did not answer questions on local moratoriums or NDAs.

records.name: Shomari Figures
records.what: At a Lowndes County event asked residents if they wanted the proposed 1,050-acre, $1.5B AI data center in Hayneville; when they said no, said 'Well, I'm with the people of Lowndes County.' Columnist reports he is not entirely opposed to hyperscale data centers but says companies need to pick sites where communities actually want them.

records.name: Dina Titus
records.what: Nevada Independent: described the permitting process she wants for data centers on federal land as 'Full environmental permitting process with consideration for water and also public consultation and hearings'.

records.name: Carrie Buck
records.what: NV Independent survey: federal government should 'make it easier to build the energy and infrastructure America needs to lead in AI'

records.name: Teresa Benitez-Thompson
records.what: NV Independent survey: does not want federal actions to prevent state or local governments from taking their own regulatory action on data centers

records.name: David Flippo
records.what: NV Independent survey: 'The best decisions are made at the most local level possible.' Opposes tax abatements; would support federal involvement only for national security protection

records.name: Susie Lee
records.what: Nevada Independent: said there should be disclosure requirements on water consumption and potentially energy efficiency standards. The article reports almost all candidates opposed a blanket federal pause on data centers.

records.name: Martin O'Donnell
records.what: NV Independent survey: supports legislation ensuring local communities are not negatively affected by data centers; backs water usage disclosure requirements

records.name: Steven Horsford
records.what: Nevada Independent: said the federal government should set standards requiring disclosure of energy and water use; states should be allowed to 'go further' ('a national standard should act as a floor we can build on, never a ceiling'). The only candidate who kept the door open to a federal moratorium in future.

records.name: Cody Whipple
records.what: Nevada Independent: written response supports 'common-sense frameworks that safeguard Nevada's natural resources while fostering technological innovation'; campaign later said he wants local water, agricultural and technology officials to inform federal standards. At a closed-door event recording he called data centers a 'national security issue for us'.

records.name: Hillary Scholten
records.what: Announced introduction of two bills, the Data Center Resource Disclosure Act (NTIA annual survey of operators' energy and water consumption, public comment, public dashboard, list of non-responders) and the Defending Our Energy and Water Act (DoD to update data center efficiency requirements and ensure new facilities adopt cooling technologies that reduce water impact). "Accountability starts with transparency."

records.name: Don Beyer
records.what: Letter urging the Fairfax County Planning Commission to deny the Edsall Data Center Substation 2232 application, citing land use, flooding mitigation, light and noise pollution and Lincolnia's growth goals: "Data center infrastructure should not be built in residential areas where its scale and likely impacts are fundamentally incompatible with the character and quality of life of adjacent neighborhoods."

records.name: Chris Van Hollen
records.what: Signed, with Sen. Alsobrooks and seven Maryland House members, a letter urging FERC to relieve Maryland ratepayers of transmission costs assigned for out-of-state data center demand and to require PJM to adopt stronger protections.
records.source_name: Rep. April McClain Delaney press release (joint delegation letter)

records.name: Angela D. Alsobrooks
records.what: Signed, with Sen. Van Hollen and seven Maryland House members, a letter urging FERC to act quickly on the Maryland Office of People's Counsel complaint and to require PJM to protect Maryland ratepayers from transmission costs assigned to them for out-of-state data center demand.
records.source_name: Rep. April McClain Delaney press release (joint delegation letter)

records.name: Jon Husted
records.what: Told Spectrum News "What we're requiring the data centers to do is to produce their own power so that the local ratepayers don't have to foot the bill," and that data-center siting decisions "should be made by local residents and local communities, not the federal government."

records.name: David McCormick
records.what: In a City & State Q&A reposted by his office, described an "AI covenant" for data centers: "You need to protect rates for the people in the community... give them rate protection or bring more energy than you use," "You need to protect the water... via a closed loop," and "The ultimate decision-making power is going to reside with the communities – township supervisors, county commissioners and the people."
records.source_name: City & State PA (via Sen. McCormick site)

records.name: Johnny Olszewski
records.what: Co-signed Maryland Congressional delegation letter to FERC urging revision of PJM cost-allocation rules so Maryland consumers do not finance $2B in infrastructure built primarily for out-of-state data centers.

records.name: Sarah Elfreth
records.what: Co-signed Maryland Congressional delegation letter to FERC urging revision of PJM cost-allocation rules so Maryland consumers do not finance $2B in infrastructure built primarily for out-of-state data centers.

records.name: Glenn Ivey
records.what: Co-signed Maryland Congressional delegation letter to FERC urging revision of PJM cost-allocation rules so Maryland consumers do not finance $2B in infrastructure built primarily for out-of-state data centers.

records.name: April McClain Delaney
records.what: Joined, and issued the press release for, the Maryland Congressional delegation letter to FERC urging revision of PJM transmission cost-allocation rules so Maryland ratepayers do not pay roughly $2 billion for infrastructure needed primarily for out-of-state data centers; letter supports the Maryland Office of People's Counsel's FERC complaint.

records.name: Kweisi Mfume
records.what: Named among the Maryland congressional delegation members calling on FERC to require PJM to protect Marylanders after PJM assigned roughly $2 billion in costs to Maryland ratepayers for infrastructure needed primarily to serve out-of-state data centers; the letter supports a complaint filed by the Maryland Office of People's Counsel.

records.name: Jamie Raskin
records.what: Co-signed Maryland Congressional delegation letter to FERC urging revision of PJM cost-allocation rules so Maryland consumers do not finance $2B in infrastructure built primarily for out-of-state data centers.

records.name: Roger Marshall
records.what: Press release applauding the expansion of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge: 'I've heard from Kansans who are concerned that infrastructure costs for data centers could be pushed onto households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms.'

records.name: Raphael G. Warnock
records.what: Wrote EPA Administrator Zeldin requesting best-practice guidance for communities protecting water supplies from data center expansion, with a written response and briefing within four weeks: "Small, rural communities have been left to negotiate on their own with multi-million-dollar corporations whose well-staffed legal teams may negotiate dozens of deals at a time." Cited OpenAI's Effingham County project and 24 Georgia local moratoria.

records.name: Cindy Hyde-Smith
records.what: At the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee's FERC oversight hearing, said Mississippi "continues to be at the forefront of safeguarding ratepayers by ensuring companies, like data centers, pay their fair share for large loads," and asked commissioners what mechanisms FERC is implementing for large-load customers to make upfront payments and minimum financial commitments to keep rates from rising.

records.name: Tim Scott
records.what: Authored a Post and Courier commentary saying data centers are vital to competitiveness and national security, that "Hardworking families and small businesses should not have higher electric bills because of the energy demands of massive global corporations," and praising Google's commitment to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to secure 100% of its added energy needs without passing costs to ratepayers.
records.source_name: The Post and Courier (op-ed by Sen. Scott)

records.name: Dan Osborn
records.what: In prepared remarks at a press conference in rural Dunbar, said “we need to be focused on building hospitals, not data centers,” commended Gov. Jim Pillen for executive orders rolling back tax incentives for data centers, and said “we must protect our water and land, not sell it to the highest bidder.”

records.name: Rashida Tlaib
records.what: Introduced the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act, which permanently bans large AI data centers and associated infrastructure on land owned or managed by the U.S., including military bases, and requires removal of existing qualifying data centers and site remediation.

records.name: Roger Marshall
records.what: At Semafor's World of Work event, said he does not want tax incentives for data centers or for them to 'drive up other people's electricity costs,' pointed to higher rates near Panasonic's Kansas plant as a warning, and said of Kansas counties' moratoriums: 'I certainly support their moratoriums,' adding those decisions belong at the local level.

records.name: Mike Lee
records.what: At the committee's FERC oversight hearing, Lee said he supported FERC's Large Load Order, called it 'not a one-size-fits-all solution,' and agreed that 'existing ratepayers should not subsidize the cost of data centers.'

records.name: James Talarico
records.what: Released a data-center plan: federal minimum requirements for the grid, environment, jobs and transparency; repeal of the Texas data center sales-tax exemption; large energy users pay for their own infrastructure and grid interconnection costs; closed-loop water systems that reuse a fixed amount of water; local authority to approve and reject projects; and release of facility-level tax-break records. He did not call for a moratorium.

records.name: Shomari Figures
records.what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), added 07/22/2026.

records.name: Gabe Evans
records.what: Introduced H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, with Rep. Kathy Castor. It directs states and their PUCs to consider standards for connecting large-load customers so those customers, not families and small businesses, cover new generation, transmission and upgrade costs. Cleared House Energy and Commerce 52-0.

records.name: Kathy Castor
records.what: Sponsor, with Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO), of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, which would require each state regulatory authority to consider a federal standard under which data centers and hyperscalers with demand of 100 megawatts pay the full cost of generation, transmission or distribution upgrades needed to serve them. Cleared the House Energy and Commerce Committee 52-0.

records.name: Lauren Underwood
records.what: Introduced H.R. 9825, the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026. Its official title: to require data center operators to submit to States or the EPA Administrator and the Secretaries of Energy and Agriculture reports on data center energy and water use. Referred to House Energy and Commerce.

records.name: Mark R. Warner
records.what: Rolled out an AI legislative agenda including the Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act, which requires large AI data centers to publicly disclose energy and water consumption, emissions, backup generation and other operational impacts, conditions federal bonus depreciation on meeting efficiency and sustainability standards, and dedicates the resulting revenue to a National Workforce Transition Fund.

records.name: Terri Sewell
records.what: Announced cosponsorship of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would stop new construction and large expansions of AI data centers until a federal framework is established; said 'The bill simply says, let's put common sense guardrails in place before this expansion continues' and 'Responsible innovation and community protection are not competing goals—they are complementary ones.'

records.name: Mark DeSaulnier
records.what: Cosponsored H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

records.name: Lori Trahan
records.what: At the Energy and Commerce markup she supported passage of the Ratepayer Protection Act and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (H.R. 6529). Said: 'If you build the data center, you pay for the data center.' Said both are 'good first steps' but 'don't fully address the water these facilities draw from our communities.'

records.name: Bob Latta
records.what: Statement on full Energy and Commerce Committee approval of H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act (July 21, 2026): said he spoke in support at the markup and that numerous states, including Ohio, already have large load tariffs in place for data centers.

records.name: Jon Husted
records.what: Introduced the Ratepayer Protection Act, which would require states to consider establishing standards for connecting large electricity users such as data centers, so that those customers pay for the generation, transmission and other infrastructure needed to serve them. “We must do that without passing the costs on to working families and small businesses.”

records.name: Sanford Bishop
records.what: Said south Georgia communities need guardrails, transparency on water/power consumption, and community benefits before data centers move forward.

records.name: Austin Scott
records.what: Said computing 'is a big part of national security' and data centers should be in the U.S.; said 'We need to make sure that the companies who build the data centers are paying their own cost of energy' and that residents see no increased power costs. Said 'Closed-loop systems don't use nearly as much water as the old systems do. We need to make sure that we're talking about what kind of cooling systems they have.'

records.name: Alan Armstrong
records.what: Promoting his American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure Act, said "A manufacturer, a data center, an industrial facility will not commit billions of dollars to a region if it cannot obtain reliable energy at a competitive price."

records.name: Tommy Tuberville
records.what: Campaigning at an Alabama Sheriffs Association event, said opponents "are listening to all this nonsense they see on social media that's coming from China because China does not want us to grow," called environmental and noise objections "bull crap," and touted data center tax revenue for schools and law enforcement.

records.name: Charles E. Schumer
records.what: Told reporters that data centers should "pay their fair share and use more clean energy" and that Democrats would pursue data-center reform if they retake the Senate, adding "We know how important they are, and we've heard the message loud and clear."

records.name: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
records.what: Issued a statement supporting Gov. Hochul's executive order pausing hyperscale data-center construction for one year, saying New Yorkers need "ironclad guarantees that their energy bills won't spike, their water will be protected, and their air will remain clean."

records.name: Emilia Sykes
records.what: Advanced the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (H.R. 9497) in the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee; the release says the bill 'advances efforts to study the impact of data centers on regional water resources' but does not attribute that provision to her.

records.name: Edward J. Markey
records.what: Released a discussion draft of the Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act, which would require a federal public-interest certificate before a data center is permitted, set minimum energy, environmental and economic standards, and fund community monitoring grants. Markey: 'Communities are organizing and demanding action to protect their air, water, energy bills, and quality of life from the tsunami of data centers around the country.'

records.name: Maxine Waters
records.what: Cosponsored H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

records.name: Jeff Van Drew
records.what: With Rep. Riley, introduced the FAIR Data Act, which prohibits utilities from passing grid upgrade costs for very large (75+ MW) data centers onto households and small businesses; said companies behind these projects should 'cover those added costs instead of passing them on to ratepayers'.

records.name: Josh Riley
records.what: Introduced the FAIR Data Act, bipartisan legislation to stop data-center projects from raising energy bills for Upstate New York families and small businesses by shielding ratepayers from the generation, transmission and distribution upgrades those projects require.

records.name: Morgan McGarvey
records.what: Sent a letter to LG&E President John Crockett III opposing the hyperscale data center planned for Camp Ground Road and demanding existing ratepayers not bear the cost; release says the 400 MW facility is a 63% increase in demand.

records.name: Morgan McGarvey
records.what: LPM reported he told a forum he opposes hyperscale data center construction in Louisville and the state, and that residents should control what gets put into their community (headline: 'absolutely opposed'; his own quoted words: 'I am done with out-of-state corporations coming into our state, our home, our community, and using our resources').

records.name: Dina Titus
records.what: Letter to BLM (sent July 8) asking for 'robust public consultation and transparency' in permitting data centers on public land; said the BLM let a developer switch from a solar farm to a data center on federal land 'without any public review. This is unacceptable.'

records.name: John R. Curtis
records.what: Told Utah News Dispatch, citing distrust after the Stratos project's quick approval through the Military Installation Development Authority, that 'we do have some real uncertainty about these data centers. What's behind the meter? What's not?' and that 'something that I want to work on at the federal level is bringing some reliable, predictable measuring techniques' so the public has standard metrics; he said the industry had 'failed' at explaining why the facilities are needed.

records.name: Ron Wyden
records.what: Co-signed with Sen. Merkley a letter to Gov. Kotek's Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee raising energy demand, consumer electricity costs, water, noise, farmland rezoning, tribal consultation and transparency.

records.name: Jeff Merkley
records.what: Co-signed with Sen. Wyden a letter to Gov. Tina Kotek's Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee asking it to consider rising energy demand, increased electricity costs for consumers, water quantity and quality, steam and noise from cooling, rezoning of agricultural land, tribal treaty consultation, and public transparency on environmental and infrastructure impacts.

records.name: Roger Marshall
records.what: Quoted in a KSHB voter guide ahead of the August 4, 2026 Kansas primary: 'Kansas isn't going to hand over our land, water, or power grid to Big Tech companies that turn a profit while local families foot the bill with taxpayer giveaways.'

records.name: Michael Whatley
records.what: Told a Fox News interview that “this opposition to data centers is not organic”, and agreed governments should offer developers tax breaks, though not subsidies, to encourage expansion.

records.name: Chuck Grassley
records.what: At a Q&A with Chesterman Company employees in Sioux City, asked about data centers, Grassley said 'These are state and local decisions to make,' and discussed their positives and negatives and possible legislation on their construction.

records.name: Brett Guthrie
records.what: Told WNKY: 'We can't have a moratorium that would cripple us. We also have to respect local communities and ensure these data centers pay their own way.' Said 'there's a good reason to be concerned' and developers should cover infrastructure costs.

records.name: Melat Kiros
records.what: Told Drop Site News she supports a moratorium on data center construction; said 'a federal data center moratorium is imperative and should be used as a negotiation tactic to implement significant regulation of AI.'

records.name: André Carson
records.what: In a release on the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (H.R. 9442, of which he is an original cosponsor) he said: 'Our bill would enact a pause until we can guarantee common sense protections.'

records.name: LaMonica McIver
records.what: Cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (sponsor Rep. Ocasio-Cortez), added 06/29/2026.

records.name: Kirsten E. Gillibrand
records.what: Asked about the proposed $19.5B STREAM data center at the STAMP site in Alabama, NY, said "People are worried about higher energy costs. They're worried about emissions. They're worried about polluting water," that communities should decide, and that developers should use closed-loop cooling and renewables rather than ratepayer-funded grid upgrades, while saying she lacked enough information to take a position on the project.

records.name: Adelita Grijalva
records.what: Original cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act.

records.name: André Carson
records.what: Listed as a cosponsor of the House AI Data Center Moratorium Act in Ocasio-Cortez's release.

records.name: Jim McGovern
records.what: Listed among the cosponsors of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, which would institute an immediate federal moratorium on construction of new data centers and expansion of existing ones until Congress passes comprehensive AI legislation.

records.name: Frank Pallone
records.what: Called for a national AI data-center moratorium at an Energy Subcommittee markup — “in favor of a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don't harm our nation's air, water, and power bills.”

records.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
records.what: Introduced the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act, a temporary prohibition on construction of new data centers and expansion of existing ones until national safeguards (including that AI does not increase electricity and utility prices) are in place; requires reporting on water, energy, wastewater and wages.

records.name: Bob Latta
records.what: Statement after chairing the June 24, 2026 subcommittee markup: "We must ensure that American families are not left footing the bill for the significant grid upgrades and increased electricity demand driven by new AI infrastructure and other large load operations."

records.name: Troy Balderson
records.what: Co-introduced H.R. 9332, the Load Forecasting Enhancement Act, directing FERC to work with state PUCs on improving electric load forecasting as demand surges from AI and data centers. Passed Energy Subcommittee.

records.name: Martin Heinrich
records.what: In a Latitude Media interview reposted by his office, said data-center developers should follow SunZia's community-first approach, that "there's a healthy dose of arrogance in some of these" proposals, and that a developer should be able to tell a community "we're actually going to be able to lower your electricity bills."

records.name: Suhas Subramanyam
records.what: Introduced, with Reps. Jay Obernolte (R-CA) and Valerie Foushee (D-NC), the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act, directing NIST in coordination with DOE to develop best practices and technical standards for measuring data center energy and water use, as a foundation for forecasting, planning and siting. "We need a simple way to track how much power and water these facilities use."

records.name: Cynthia M. Lummis
records.what: Introduced the POWER Up Act, which amends the Federal Power Act to clarify FERC jurisdiction over the interconnection of large-load facilities (projected peak demand of 100 MW or more) to interstate transmission, requires FERC to issue standardized interconnection procedures within 18 months, and explicitly preserves state and local jurisdiction over siting, permitting, construction, retail rates, local distribution and generation. Lummis: 'When a facility wants to draw as much power as a city, that is not an ordinary retail question. It is a grid question.'

records.name: Elizabeth Warren
records.what: Sent letters to KKR, BlackRock, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Blackstone asking for details of their data center investments and how they ensure Americans are not left paying for them, with responses due June 27.

records.name: Marsha Blackburn
records.what: Posted a video questioning the location of DC Blox's proposed data center next to the Nashville Zoo and calling on the developer to 'revisit this placement,' while making clear she supports data centers more broadly.

records.name: John R. Curtis
records.what: Told Roll Call, on the Utah data-center uproar, 'I have almost no data on the water usage. I've heard it's closed-loop, but I don't know that,' called siting 'a local issue,' and said he was open to a congressional certification system for AI facilities similar to LEED building standards.

records.name: Brett Guthrie
records.what: Signed a letter with Reps. Joyce and Latta to the PCAST co-chairs and FBI Director Kash Patel expressing worries about 'foreign influence campaigns targeting artificial intelligence'; told the Daily News there is 'reasonable suspicion' that opposition is backed by China.

records.name: Tom Cotton
records.what: Wrote Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche asking DOJ to investigate alleged Chinese Communist Party-linked funding of U.S. nonprofits producing anti-data-center content, while stating "Americans certainly have valid concerns about potential rising energy costs and strains on natural resources related to data centers" but "we can't allow any effort by foreign adversaries to extort these fears and undermine our technological development."

records.name: Derek Schmidt
records.what: Per Ranson Financial's summary of a CJonline report: at a town hall gave three tips for communities: developers should not require tax abatements; data centers should source power from new or supplemental sources to avoid raising local utility costs; modern data centers can be designed as closed systems that do not consume large amounts of water.

records.name: Edward J. Markey
records.what: Reintroduced with Rep. Beyer the AI Environmental Impacts Act of 2026, requiring AI data centers to report environmental and energy impacts with fines for non-compliance, NIST measurement standards, and an EPA lifecycle study.

records.name: Bob Latta
records.what: Co-signed, with Chairmen Guthrie and Joyce, a letter to the PCAST co-chairs and FBI Director Kash Patel requesting information about evidence suggesting foreign influence campaigns are working to slow American AI progress and block data center infrastructure.

records.name: Mark Warner
records.what: Cosponsored the Power for the People Act, joining Sens. Van Hollen, Durbin, Blumenthal, Booker, Duckworth, Smith, Welch and Alsobrooks. Per his office, the bill directs states to evaluate the need for new rate classes for data centers, directs FERC to issue a rule ensuring data centers pay for the local transmission upgrades they require, sets up interconnection incentives tied to bringing new generation and storage, clean energy and prevailing wages, and provides resources to improve load forecasting. Warner: “If corporations are going to run data centers in Virginia, they should cover the cost of them.”

records.name: Raul Ruiz
records.what: Letter to the Imperial County Board of Supervisors, read into the record by a district representative on June 2: "I unequivocally oppose data centers in Imperial Valley and urge local officials to prevent them from happening." Cited reduced life expectancy, air pollution, asthma, energy costs and water use. His office said he plans to send letters to EPA and DOE seeking federal oversight and environmental review of proposed projects in water-stressed environmental justice communities, including the Imperial and Coachella valleys.

records.name: Mike Lee
records.what: Told E&E News he had no immediate plans to take up data-center legislation: 'I don't currently have that identified as a priority,' while saying he was 'happy to look at' the Ratepayer Protection Act.

records.name: Chuck Fleischmann
records.what: As chair of the House Energy and Water Development Appropriations Subcommittee, said 'there will be no rate increases without going to the people' regarding TVA rate changes tied to data center demand.

records.name: Ben McAdams
records.what: UT-1 Democratic debate: all four candidates opposed the Stratos Project; said 'What we need are federal standards to make sure that when, as the economy is transformed, that the American people are the ones who benefit'. Opponents pointed to his financial stake in a data center project near Delta in Millard County; he said he was 'the only candidate who has worked to make a data center better by adding renewable energy' and described the stake as stock options and consulting pay from two years ago.

records.name: Gabe Vasquez
records.what: Told Source NM he encourages the county to approve the temporary moratorium it was considering on the proposed Socorro County data center, saying the proposal “should not be considered at this time.”

records.name: Luke Bronin
records.what: The American Prospect wrote that, despite donations from billionaires with a stake in the data center build-out, Bronin “has called for regulation requiring data center developers to pay their fair share.” The article does not quote him or say where he said it.

records.name: Adam B. Schiff
records.what: Introduced the Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act: large-load facilities pay 100% of network upgrade costs, must demonstrate demand flexibility and provide their own power to interconnect, FERC to enable non-firm transmission service, and stronger interconnection screening against speculative projects. Schiff: "Hard-working Americans should not be left to foot the tab for rising energy costs. There needs to be guardrails that protect Americans' pocketbooks."

records.name: Katie Boyd Britt
records.what: Introduced the Advancing Water Reuse Act (S. 3585) with Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-NM): a tax credit for on-site water recycling at "manufacturing, food processing, and other industrial entities, including data center facilities"; Britt's statement cites water demand from "advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, and other growth industries."
records.source_name: Sen. Luján press release (joint with Britt)

records.name: Ben Ray Luján
records.what: Introduced with Sen. Katie Britt the Advancing Water Reuse Act, a 30% investment tax credit for onsite water recycling systems at "manufacturing, food processing, and other industrial entities, including data center facilities," to replace freshwater/groundwater draws with recycled water.

records.name: Suhas Subramanyam
records.what: Introduced the Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act, directing DHS to produce a security strategy and recommendations for protecting communities around data centers, considering the security of transmission and water infrastructure.

records.name: Ruben Gallego
records.what: Told reporters in Phoenix data centers are a "necessary evil" for the AI race but "Your local resident should be held harmless. We shouldn't be paying more in electricity bills because data centers are here"; called for rolling back Arizona's 2013 data center tax exemption, said some data centers "end up paying, on average, less than some of the homeowners who are right next to them," and "I fear that we may not have enough water and we may not have enough power generation to be able to hold harmless everyone else."

records.name: Ben McAdams
records.what: Posted that 'Utah should welcome technology investment only when it aligns with our values: water stewardship, Great Salt Lake restoration, clean energy, transparency, public accountability, and real public benefit. This proposed data center project in Box Elder County does not meet that standard.'

records.name: Ron Wyden
records.what: Sent letters to the CEOs of Google, Apple, Meta and Amazon demanding answers on data-center water impacts in drought-prone Oregon (over 100 data centers), asking about closed-loop cooling, groundwater withdrawal, contaminant mitigation, public water tracking and community transparency, with a May 29 response deadline.

records.name: Chellie Pingree
records.what: Cosponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026 (sponsor Rep. Tonko), added 04/30/2026.

records.name: Julie Fedorchak
records.what: At the Energy Subcommittee hearing 'AI and the Grid: Meeting Growing Power Demand While Protecting Ratepayers,' emphasized that those who drive the need for new energy infrastructure should pay for it (press release paraphrase), asked witnesses whether large loads such as data centers have shown willingness to pay for upgrades, and highlighted her FAIR Act and High-Capacity Grid Act.

records.name: Shelley Moore Capito
records.what: Said data-center companies must have early and strong community engagement and that 'transparency about the process and the effects on local residents could go a long way'; said proposed projects plan to build their own power, which 'could actually maybe improve the situation because there will be excess power probably created,' and that water drawn from the Ohio would be replenished and cleaned.

records.name: Steven Horsford
records.what: Release announced he would join OpenAI and Rep. Khanna at a College of Southern Nevada AI workforce-training event; says he helped secure almost $7 million for CSN's Westside Education and Training Center.

records.name: Nick Begich III
records.what: Op-ed: said Alaska's natural gas, renewables and stranded energy assets are an advantage for AI data centers; said the DATA Act protects ratepayers from subsidizing new loads; wrote 'We can hesitate, regulate too early and risk becoming an observer... or we can engage thoughtfully, strategically and on our own terms.'

records.name: André Carson
records.what: Original cosponsor (04/23/2026) of H.R. 8488, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026, sponsored by Rep. McIver. Its text requires developers, 180 days before a definitive step, to disclose the site location and estimated resource needs and environmental impact to local elected officials and the public, and limits non-disclosure agreements.

records.name: LaMonica McIver
records.what: Introduced H.R. 8488, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026 (04/23/2026). Its text requires developers, 180 days before a definitive step, to disclose the site location and estimated resource needs and environmental impact to local elected officials and the public, limits non-disclosure agreements, and requires a developer-funded independent environmental impact analysis.

records.name: Mark R. Warner
records.what: Dismissed the proposed data-center moratorium as 'idiocy' at an Axios event, per E&E News.

records.name: Tim Kaine
records.what: Told E&E News he opposes a data-center moratorium: 'I think a moratorium would send the message to other nations, "Hey, the U.S. is giving up leadership in this space," and I don't want to send that message.'

records.name: Nick Begich III
records.what: Introduced the DATA Act of 2026 with Reps. Crenshaw and Owens; the release says it lets manufacturers and other energy-intensive industries run fully isolated off-grid power so 'innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands.'

records.name: Jon Ossoff
records.what: Sent a letter to FERC Chairman Laura Swett opening an inquiry into whether AI data center growth is raising Georgians' power bills, asking how FERC will ensure technology companies "pay their own way" and what it will do if data center construction raises utility costs beyond predictions; cited the Georgia PSC's December 2025 approval of 9,885 MW of new Georgia Power generation for large loads and said Georgians are "suffering from sky-high power bills." Response requested by June 1, 2026. Georgia PSC commissioners publicly disputed the premise.

records.name: Jon Ossoff
records.what: Wrote to FERC Chair Laura Swett asking, among other questions, whether FERC considers it credible or enforceable when technology companies say they will “pay their own way” for data center power, what it is doing to improve load forecasting, and how it will take part in standardising interconnection for large loads such as data centers.

records.name: Elizabeth Warren
records.what: With Sen. Hawley, wrote to the EIA administrator in March 2026 asking for a mandatory annual energy-use survey of data centers and other large loads; EIA then announced a mandatory data center survey to be completed by September 30, 2026. Warren: 'Americans deserve to know how much energy data centers are sucking up and what that's doing to their utility bills.'

records.name: Kweisi Mfume
records.what: Original cosponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026, sponsored by Rep. Tonko; congress.gov gives its purpose as promoting data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes to mitigate the impact of data centers on other electricity consumers.

records.name: Paul Tonko
records.what: Sponsor of H.R. 8241, the Power for the People Act of 2026, introduced 04/09/2026. congress.gov gives its purpose as promoting data center load queues and data center-specific rate classes to mitigate the impact of data centers on other electricity consumers.

records.name: Rick Scott
records.what: Introduced, with Sen. Roger Marshall, a concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge — under which tech companies commit to cover their own electricity and grid-infrastructure costs — is sound national policy. Scott: "Big Data centers are already putting a substantial financial burden on American families... Florida families shouldn't be supporting Big Tech companies' expansions with their electricity bills."

records.name: Roger Marshall
records.what: Introduced with Sen. Rick Scott a concurrent resolution supporting the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which tech companies commit to pay their own electricity and grid-infrastructure costs. Marshall: 'Kansans shouldn't have to pay higher utility bills so that big tech companies can power their data centers.'
records.source_name: Sen. Rick Scott press release (joint with Marshall)

records.name: Richard Blumenthal
records.what: As Ranking Member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, wrote public utility regulators in all 50 states requesting documents on non-disclosure agreements or other restrictions that keep data centers' energy use, water access, infrastructure strain and economic effects from public view: "American families deserve full transparency over Big Tech's expansion of data centers across the country and in their communities."

records.name: Mark Kelly
records.what: At the American AI Festival previewed unnamed legislation to "Bring developers and communities together at the beginning to work through the details—what a project means for energy, water, infrastructure, and jobs—and put real commitments on the table," with public input, enforceable agreements, local hiring and utility-rate protections.

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: With Sen. Warren, wrote EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey asking for a mandatory annual reporting requirement for data centers and other large loads covering hourly/annual/peak consumption, rates paid, upfront payments, demand response, and how transmission upgrade costs are allocated; response requested by April 9, 2026.

records.name: Martin Heinrich
records.what: At a Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing on the power grid, said "new large loads, especially data centers, must bear the costs associated with them coming online" rather than shifting them to other ratepayers, and that 1% demand flexibility from large loads could unlock 126 GW of capacity.

records.name: Ruben Gallego
records.what: Co-leads (with Padilla, Hickenlooper, Cortez Masto, King) a draft Senate Energy Democrats transmission bill expanding FERC transmission authority; the senators' release does not mention data centers, though press coverage frames it as addressing AI data center demand.

records.name: Richard J. Durbin
records.what: Introduced the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act (S. 4213), requiring data center operators to report energy and water consumption to their states, prospective facilities to report five-year estimates, and states to aggregate the data for EPA, DOE and USDA, with EPA fines for non-compliance. Durbin: 'If you've noticed a sharp increase in your utility bills lately, it may be from the growth of energy-hungry data centers.'

records.name: Bernard Sanders
records.what: Announced the Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act of 2026 with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez: a federal moratorium on new or expanded AI data centers until Congress enacts safeguards ensuring AI does not increase 'electricity or utility prices, harm communities or destroy the environment'; introduced as S.4214.

records.name: Greg Landsman
records.what: Introduced H.R. 8033, the No Harm Data Centers Act; official title: to ensure that American families are protected from the impacts of data centers on the electric grid. Referred to House Energy and Commerce.

records.name: Marsha Blackburn
records.what: Released a discussion draft of the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act that 'directs the U.S. Secretary of Energy to enter into agreements with owners and operators of data centers to protect consumers from rate increases and adverse impacts of data center development'; entities that decline become ineligible for federal incentives the Secretary identifies.

records.name: Mike Levin
records.what: With Rep. Sean Casten, led 120 House Democrats in introducing the Energy Bills Relief Act, which Levin said "ensures that data centers and large energy users pay their fair share instead of passing those costs onto families and small businesses."

records.name: Sean Casten
records.what: Co-led, with Rep. Mike Levin, the introduction by 120 House Democrats of the Energy Bills Relief Act; release lists 'Ensuring that facilities like data centers are paying for their own costs because it's not fair for their expenses to be pushed onto your household'. Casten's own quoted remarks do not mention data centers.

records.name: Bernie Moreno
records.what: Issued a release urging Carlyle Group to relinquish a $4.5M Ohio subsidy for Ark Data Centers' Akron/Independence expansion (10 jobs), sign the Ratepayer Protection Pledge and commit to more jobs, saying "When corporations like Carlyle demand massive amounts of electricity to fund their projects, it's everyday Ohioans who get stuck with the bill."

records.name: Chris Van Hollen
records.what: With Sens. Whitehouse and Heinrich, sent letters to Meta, OpenAI, xAI, Fermi America, American Intelligence & Power, Joule, Crusoe and Fundamental Data about twelve planned gas-powered data center projects, asking why they rely on gas, whether they will capture CO2, and their expected returns; responses due March 27.

records.name: Chris Van Hollen
records.what: At a Maryland delegation meeting on energy affordability: 'the surge of data center development across our region is only making things worse' and 'Consumers should not have to pay one dime in additional electricity costs to support data centers for the richest companies on the planet.'

records.name: Edward J. Markey
records.what: Led a letter with Sens. Blumenthal, Van Hollen and Booker to the president of NARUC urging state utility commissions to reject rate filings that shift data center costs onto households and small businesses.

records.name: Chris Van Hollen
records.what: Signed the Markey-led letter to the president of NARUC urging state utility commissions to reject rate filings that shift data center costs onto households and small businesses.

records.name: Cory A. Booker
records.what: Signed a letter with Sens. Markey, Blumenthal and Van Hollen to NARUC president Ann Rendahl urging state public utility commissions to reject rate filings that force residential and small-business ratepayers to subsidize AI data centers and to adopt protective policies coordinated with utilities, grid operators and federal regulators.

records.name: Adelita Grijalva
records.what: Cosponsored H.R. 7858, the Data Center Community Impact Act.

records.name: Rob Menendez
records.what: Listed as a cosponsor of the Data Center Community Impact Act, which would authorize a federal study of data centers' environmental, economic and public health impacts.

records.name: Summer Lee
records.what: Cosponsored H.R. 7858, the Data Center Community Impact Act.

records.name: Jon Husted
records.what: Attended a White House roundtable with President Trump, Energy Secretary Wright and tech executives at which Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft committed to the Ratepayer Protection Pledge to fund their own data-center power; Husted said "Requiring companies to fund their own power protects working people from higher bills."

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: Told Missourinet "I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply," and that he does not want bills rising because "some corporation came in and sucked up all the power."

records.name: Ted Budd
records.what: At a Washington Post Live event said the U.S. needs to add about 85 gigawatts a year to keep pace with demand and "that goes back to permitting reform," that "power is good" and the country needs more energy, that data-center construction decisions should be made "at a local level," and was skeptical of Sen. Sanders' moratorium proposal while saying he would need to read the text.

records.name: Rich McCormick
records.what: Opening statement as chairman at the hearing 'Powering America's AI Future: Assessing Policy Options to Increase Data Center Infrastructure': called the Trump executive order prioritizing data center permitting 'a positive step', said several projects have faced substantial permitting hurdles, and asked whether a permitting framework 'largely designed in the 1970s' is suited to this infrastructure; also raised the question of whether residential ratepayers could end up subsidizing upgrades that primarily serve high-intensity users.

records.name: Emilia Sykes
records.what: At the House Science Committee hearing on data center infrastructure said: "We need to put strong guardrails in place so that data centers support our communities rather than the other way around. Ohioans should not pay higher electricity bills so billionaires in Silicon Valley can see higher profits." Noted Ohio has 217 data centers, the fifth most of any state.

records.name: Dan Sullivan
records.what: In his annual address to the Alaska Legislature, said he is pressing for "new federal data centers on Air Force bases in Alaska for AI computing," which he said would help the military, raise domestic demand for Alaska gas and lower the cost of building and financing the gas pipeline; noted the Air Force had issued a request for information on Alaska data centers the day before at his urging.
records.source_name: Sen. Sullivan press release (address to Legislature)

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: Introduced the Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers (GRID) Act with Sen. Blumenthal, requiring data centers to obtain power from sources separate from the grid (10-year transition for existing facilities), giving consumers grid priority, and requiring public disclosure of electricity use; said "American families should not have to shoulder the burden of rising electricity costs produced by data centers."

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: Told St. Louis Public Radio, on introducing the GRID Act, that tech companies "can absolutely afford to pay for their own electricity, and they should," and that residents cannot know a project's effect on them "if they don't know exactly what the drawdown on power is going to be."

records.name: Emilia Sykes
records.what: Released the Affordability Agenda with the New Democrat Coalition; its energy section includes 'Reallocate electric grid costs to protect consumers from price hikes due to manufacturing and data center development.'

records.name: Steve Daines
records.what: Chairing a Senate Foreign Relations subcommittee hearing on European energy reform, said "whether it be for data centers, manufacturing, or defense production, reliable power is the backbone of our future prosperity."

records.name: John Boozman
records.what: At a Senate Environment and Public Works hearing on permitting reform, highlighted AI and cloud investments including the West Memphis data center and said "Arkansas was able to land these investments in part because of a reliable, affordable, and an all-the-above energy supply, including solar energy," backing permitting reform.

records.name: Sheldon Whitehouse
records.what: With Sen. Reed and four other New England senators, wrote ISO New England asking how it will shield residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases; said "As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs."

records.name: Edward J. Markey
records.what: Led a letter from six New England senators to ISO New England asking how it will protect residential ratepayers from price increases driven by data center expansion. Markey: 'As the ones who stand to benefit most, the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.'

records.name: Jack Reed
records.what: With Sen. Whitehouse, Sen. Welch and three other New England senators, wrote ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada asking what strategies the grid operator will use to protect residential customers from data-center-driven price increases; Reed said "We believe it is necessary to require tech companies, not American families, to foot the bill for their load."

records.name: Peter Welch
