records.what: Signed, with Sens. Markey, Shaheen, Blumenthal, Reed and Whitehouse, a letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada asking how the grid operator will protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases, stating 'the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.'

records.name: James C. Justice
records.what: Press release applauding American Power and Intelligence Corporation's multi-billion-dollar data center and microgrid campus in Mason County, a project he first announced with Fidelis New Energy as governor in 2023: 'I truly could not be prouder to see the seeds of our work from years ago begin to bloom.'

records.name: Jeanne Shaheen
records.what: Signed, with Sens. Welch, Blumenthal, Reed, Markey, and Whitehouse, a letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada requesting the strategies ISO-NE plans to protect residential ratepayers from data-center-driven price increases, arguing that the AI industry, not families, should bear those costs.

records.name: Elizabeth Warren
records.what: Released the companies' responses: Google committed to pay for all electricity it uses and contribute to growth-related costs; Microsoft, CoreWeave and Equinix backed separate rate classes for data centers. Warren: 'These commitments do not explain how Big Tech companies – not American consumers – will bear the full cost of data centers.'

records.name: Ron Johnson
records.what: Told Wisconsin Watch that data centers' impact on the state's electrical grid is a 'very serious concern,' adding he is unsure local officials have 'really factored it in properly.'

records.name: Tammy Baldwin
records.what: Told Wisconsin Watch: 'The developers of these need to have commitments to the local community that they won't see, that they won't have to shoulder the costs of the energy use and water use by these data centers,' and said any data-center moratorium should first be considered by the state Legislature.

records.name: Raphael G. Warnock
records.what: Secured $50 million in the FY2026 government funding law to help communities address energy and water pressures from resource-intensive projects including data centers: "This bipartisan legislation will help give Georgians and Americans relief from the energy and water pressures of new resource-intensive projects."

records.name: Cory Booker
records.what: Joined Sen. Chris Van Hollen and colleagues in introducing the Power for the People Act. Per his office, it directs states to evaluate the need for new rate classes for data centers, directs FERC to issue a rule making data centers pay for the local transmission upgrades they require, creates interconnection incentives for data centers to bring their own new generation and battery storage, and sets prevailing-wage and apprenticeship standards.

records.name: Tina Smith
records.what: Named as an original cosponsor of Sen. Van Hollen's Power for the People Act, which directs states to evaluate data-center rate classes, instructs FERC to ensure data centers pay for local transmission upgrades, and creates an interconnection system pushing data centers to offset grid impact with new generation and storage under labor standards.

records.name: Mike Levin
records.what: Introduced, with Rep. Kathy Castor, the Stopping Hikes In Electricity from Large Load Demands (SHIELD) Act: a separate rate class for large load customers (facilities using more than 75MW) so households do not pay for their grid upgrades, plus priority interconnection for large loads powered by zero-emission electricity. "Families should not be forced to subsidize massive energy costs for billion-dollar companies."

records.name: Tom Cotton
records.what: Introduced the DATA Act of 2026, which would exempt new isolated electricity generation and supply systems built to serve new loads (manufacturers, data centers and other energy-intensive industries) from certain federal regulation so they can operate independent of the existing grid. Cotton: "American dominance in artificial intelligence and other crucial emerging industries should not come at the expense of Arkansans paying higher energy costs."

records.name: Abdul El-Sayed
records.what: Released a framework for evaluating data center proposals that, as Planet Detroit described it, outlines community protections to ensure projects do not result in electric rate hikes, harm energy reliability, pollute local waterways or undermine clean-energy laws, and calls for assurances on transparency, community benefits and job-creation promises. He said he wants it to guide local decisions and federal legislation.

records.name: Rob Menendez
records.what: Co-introduced the PRICE Act (require data centers to generate the electricity they consume; 75% renewable by 2035, 100% by 2040) and the Data Center Transparency Act (EPA quarterly and EIA semi-annual data collection) with Rep. Casar.

records.name: Greg Casar
records.what: Co-introduced the PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act with Rep. Menendez; quoted: 'Families should not pay more for utilities so that billionaires can get rich off AI data centers' and 'AI data centers should not be allowed to jack up your electric bill or poison your environment.'

records.name: Raphael G. Warnock
records.what: With Sen. Markey and five other senators, wrote FERC Chair Laura Swett urging the commission to prevent data center demand from producing unjust or unreasonable electricity cost increases for households, warning AI and crypto data centers could add over 10,000 MW of demand with costs passed to residential ratepayers.

records.name: Michael F. Bennet
records.what: Campaign energy platform: "Massive energy users like data centers shouldn't drive up utility bills for Colorado families"; would "require new data centers to cover the cost of the energy they consume and to help finance the infrastructure they need," and require new projects to align with Colorado's clean energy, emissions, water conservation and workforce goals.

records.name: Catherine Cortez Masto
records.what: Submitted a $1,570,000 FY2027 community project request for the Desert Research Institute's Computing Infrastructure Evaluation Tool, "a cost-benefit framework to help Nevadans weigh trade-offs of rapid data center growth, considering water and energy resources, economic stability, and community well-being," plus $2,107,000 for a UNLV Energy Platform for Data Centers research project.
records.source_name: Sen. Cortez Masto FY2027 community project requests

records.name: Dan S. Sullivan
records.what: Petitioned to place data centers on Air Force and military installations.

records.name: Mike Collins
records.what: Told voters he recognises the importance of Georgia's more than 200 data centers but would rather let local leaders decide whether one is the right fit: “I am a firm believer in local control. If a data center goes into a local community and destroys the infrastructure, you didn't do good.” He also said there is a role for the federal government “because we're in a race with China for AI.”

records.name: Josh Turek
records.what: Framed his campaign around opposing billionaires and large corporations and embraced local moratorium sentiment; no detailed data-center platform published.

records.name: Ashley Hinson
records.what: Emphasised American AI leadership and competition with China; no specific data-center restrictions stated.

records.name: Troy Jackson
records.what: Set conditions for data centers: good-paying union jobs, fair tax payment, environmental protection, local community engagement, and covering their own power costs.

records.name: Susan Collins
records.what: Voiced concern about data-center energy consumption and cost pressure and toured redevelopment sites with Energy Secretary Chris Wright, while blaming rising rates on Democratic state leaders.

records.name: Michael Whatley
records.what: An NBC News report that he backs data-center tax breaks while owning stock in data-center companies, as republished by the North Carolina Democratic Party, his opponent's party. The NBC original has not been read.

records.name: Brian Schatz
records.what: In an interview on the Volts podcast, agreed ('100%') with the proposal that data centers needing grid capacity should fund distributed solar, storage and heat pumps on homes, and said it would be 'a rounding error' for highly profitable AI firms to also fund carbon dioxide removal.

records.name: Marsha Blackburn
records.what: Unveiled the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act national AI framework, which 'requires data center operators to be responsible for the full cost of all energy and water infrastructure needed for their operation, including construction, maintenance, and upgrades with no impact on ratepayers.'

records.name: Ruben Gallego
records.what: On the Volts podcast discussing his energy plan, said that if data centers strain the grid "the resident and the small business owner should not be having to pay the differential caused by these companies," that legislation should ensure "the individual consumer will be held harmless" while the large-load customer pays the difference, and that data centers should "bring your own energy" such as SMRs rather than restarting old coal or gas plants.

records.name: Richard Blumenthal
records.what: With Sens. Warren and Van Hollen, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and three other companies probing whether "tech companies are passing on the costs of building and operating their data centers to ordinary Americans," including who bears grid-upgrade costs if the AI boom subsides.
records.source_name: Sen. Warren press office (in the news)

records.name: Elizabeth Warren
records.what: With Sens. Van Hollen and Blumenthal, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix asking how they will keep data center grid costs off consumers' bills. Warren: 'Through these utility price increases, American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies.'

records.name: Chris Van Hollen
records.what: With Sens. Warren and Blumenthal, sent letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix asking how they will prevent data center grid costs from being passed to consumers.

records.name: Rashida Tlaib
records.what: Statement after Southfield City Council approved a site plan for Metrobloks' proposed AI data center: cited residents' concerns about electricity costs rising 'by as much as 267%' and consuming 'millions of gallons of water per day', said she was inspired to see residents 'organizing together to push back', and said she would work with them to 'protect our communities'.

records.name: Maria Cantwell
records.what: Asked about environmental groups' call for a data-center moratorium, Cantwell said advocates 'should call for an above-all energy plan that allows for the construction of renewables to play into that demand for the future,' adding 'we're growing, so we need more energy sources.'

records.name: Greg Landsman
records.what: Introduced H.R. 6529, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act, whose official title is to require FERC to hold a technical conference on protecting residential ratepayers from increased costs associated with large loads. Ordered to be reported by House Energy and Commerce on 07/21/2026.

records.name: Chellie Pingree
records.what: Spokesperson Gabrielle Maninno said Pingree believes Congress has a responsibility to assess the environmental and consumer impacts of data center and AI expansion and put 'strong, science-based protections in place'.

records.name: Ruben Gallego
records.what: Announcing his energy plan, said utilities are mostly regulated at the state and local level but the "federal government can invest in technology to divert energy from data centers during lulls in demand."

records.name: Derrick Van Orden
records.what: Told Wisconsin Watch: “The average Wisconsinite should not have to subsidize the power or water for a commercial entity” (said of manufacturers’ energy and water use, in a Foxconn story), and, of data centers, that they are “either going to help pay for those utility rates (that) are rising, or you’re going to self-power.”

records.name: Martin Heinrich
records.what: With Sen. Mike Lee, sent a bipartisan letter urging FERC to take up DOE's Section 403 proposal for a rulemaking on large-load interconnection; Heinrich called it "a step in the right direction" and said the rule should "ensure that households aren't left covering the increased demand from large new energy users."

records.name: Christopher A. Coons
records.what: Introduced the Liquid Cooling for AI Act (with Sen. Dave McCormick): GAO to assess R&D needs for liquid cooling in data centers, DOE to report recommendations, and an industry advisory body; the release cites LBNL's finding that data centers used 4.4% of U.S. electricity in 2023 and could reach 12.8% by 2028. Coons: "Leading the world in AI innovation shouldn't have to mean skyrocketing energy bills for American families or giving up ground in the fight against climate change."

records.name: Adam B. Schiff
records.what: Co-signed letter with Sens. Markey, Van Hollen, Warren, Welch, Blumenthal and Warnock to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging the agency to ensure increased energy demand from data centers does not result in unjust or unreasonable rate hikes for American households.

records.name: Kevin Mullin
records.what: Led a group of 20 House members in a letter to FERC, Edison Electric Institute, and the Data Center Coalition expressing concern that data center energy costs are being passed onto consumers and requesting information on consumer protections.

records.name: Debbie Dingell
records.what: Named among the co-signers of the Mullin-led letters to FERC, the Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition raising concern that energy costs associated with data center development 'are increasingly being passed on to everyday Americans and small businesses' and requesting information.

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: After Missouri Senate President Pro Tem Cindy O'Laughlin called his data-center concerns misleading, said she "told me to stop asking questions about data centers and higher electricity rates. Not a chance."

records.name: Josh Hawley
records.what: Sent a letter to Ameren CEO Martin Lyons asking whether Ameren analyzed how discounted data-center contracts will affect residential prices and whether it prioritized household rate stability, saying Missourians "should not be forced to subsidize corporate projects while struggling to keep their lights on."

records.name: Michael F. Bennet
records.what: Co-signed (with Hickenlooper and four House members) a letter to Energy Secretary Wright on cancelled Colorado energy projects stating: "In an era where artificial intelligence and data centers are driving a rise in energy demand, we must meet these challenges by investing in responsible and affordable energy solutions, rather than destabilizing them."

records.name: Ted Cruz
records.what: Press release after touring Oracle and OpenAI's Stargate AI data center in Abilene: 'Texas is leading the way to make sure the United States beats China in the AI race. This is the beginning of a long-term effort to invest in American jobs, supply the additional power needed for AI, and deliver products and services that will benefit all Americans.'

records.name: Cynthia M. Lummis
records.what: Op-ed in Cowboy State Daily arguing Wyoming baseload energy should power U.S. AI data centers ('If we don't power America's AI with Wyoming energy, China will build their AI dominance on their coal instead'), citing 100 MW-plus AI training clusters; it does not address ratepayer or community impacts.

records.name: Troy Balderson
records.what: Led H.R. 1047, the GRID Power Act, directing FERC to let grid operators fast-track dispatchable power projects through interconnection queues. Cited data center growth in central Ohio. Passed the House.

records.name: Mark Kelly
records.what: Released the "AI for America" roadmap, noting data center power use could reach up to 12% of national electricity demand and proposing an AI Horizon Fund financed by AI companies; "As AI companies thrive, they must be good partners and invest in our workers, our economy, and our energy future."

records.name: Blake Moore
records.what: Introduced bipartisan 'Unleashing Low-Cost Rural AI Act' requiring DOE, Interior, and Agriculture to study how AI data center expansions impact rural America — energy supply, reliability, consumer costs, and infrastructure

records.name: Susie Lee
records.what: Toured Switch AI factory in Las Vegas with Democratic Leader Jeffries; said 'Switch is bringing the cutting edge of AI innovation right here to southern Nevada' and that the factories 'will help create good-paying jobs'.

records.name: John Barrasso
records.what: Senate floor speech praising the Trump AI Action Plan because 'it tears down barriers to building new data centers,' arguing that data centers need steady, reliable power and that more American energy means data centers grow in America rather than overseas.

records.name: Martin Heinrich
records.what: At a July 2025 ENR hearing on electricity demand growth, questioned Vantage Data Centers EVP Jeff Tench about how Interior Department reviews delaying wind and solar on federal land affect data-center business and grid reliability.

records.name: Andy Kim
records.what: Introduced with Sen. Tim Sheehy the Advanced Reactor Modernization for Operational Resilience (ARMOR) Act of 2025, which authorizes up to 50-year military contracts for power from advanced nuclear reactors and, per the release, encourages "the co-location of AI infrastructure and data centers" at those installations.

records.name: Mike Lee
records.what: Chaired a Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing on surging electricity demand, saying 'America's electricity demand is surging. We're entering a new era driven by data centers, AI computing, electric vehicles, and manufacturing returning home.'
records.source_name: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee release

records.name: David McCormick
records.what: Hosted the Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit with President Trump, where companies announced more than $90 billion in data-center, energy and workforce investments (CoreWeave $6B Lancaster, Blackstone $25B NE PA, ECP $5B York); the fact sheet mentions no ratepayer or community safeguards.

records.name: Rob Wittman
records.what: Supported the FY2026 NDAA committee text that “directs the Navy to use a promising partnership between Naval Weapons Station Yorktown and Dominion Energy as a pathfinder to determine how to leverage nuclear power to meet Navy and Marine Corps installation power demands, in addition to supporting the data center energy demands of accelerating technologies like artificial intelligence.”

records.name: Brian Schatz
records.what: Senate floor remarks: 'Energy demand is soaring for the first time in decades, largely not exclusively, but largely because of AI data centers,' arguing wind and solar are the fastest way to meet that demand; no position on who pays.

records.name: Cory A. Booker
records.what: Co-led, with Sen. Andy Kim and seven NJ House members, a letter to PJM Interconnection ahead of a ~17% June 2025 rate increase; the letter says the 2024 capacity auction results "reflect the growing demand on the grid from data centers and advanced computer technology" and asks PJM what it is doing to lower rates, speed interconnection and prevent future price spikes.

records.name: Andy Kim
records.what: Co-led, with Sen. Booker and seven NJ House members, a letter to PJM Interconnection ahead of a ~17% June 2025 rate increase; the letter attributes the 2024 capacity auction results to "the growing demand on the grid from data centers and advanced computer technology" and asks PJM what it is doing to lower rates, speed interconnection and prevent future price spikes.

records.name: Troy Balderson
records.what: At Energy and Commerce hearing, noted his district hosts Google, AWS, Meta, QTS, Vantage and others, with signed power agreements reaching 5,000 MW by 2030. Questioned Eric Schmidt about tech companies' role in bringing new generation capacity online.

records.name: Brett Guthrie
records.what: Washington Times op-ed (posted by E&C): argued for expanded energy production for AI data centers and permitting reform, warned about China; said 'common-sense, tailored protections may be necessary'.

records.name: Julie Fedorchak
records.what: Announced the next step of her AI and Energy Working Group, an RFI on AI energy demand with a topic titled 'Strategic Competition: Outpacing China.' Said: 'To be AI dominant, we must first be energy dominant.'

records.name: John Thune
records.what: Floor remarks 'Energy Security is National Security' warned that 'the boom in data center construction – in particular to power the rise of artificial intelligence – is placing, and will place, vast new demands upon the grid,' arguing for more conventional energy supply.
records.source_name: Senate Majority Leader Thune floor remarks

records.name: Mark Kelly
records.what: Co-signed a letter (with Sens. Van Hollen, Booker and Kaine) asking FERC to "host a technical conference" on ensuring sufficient new generation for data center demand while keeping rates affordable and respecting state energy policy.

records.name: Sheldon Whitehouse
records.what: Led a letter with Sens. Schatz, Welch, Markey and Warren urging the Biden White House to reconsider a proposed executive order fast-tracking AI data-center construction, asking it to keep clean air and water standards and not prioritize tech companies' energy needs over households; said large companies "should not" be relieved of bringing new clean energy "while passing higher energy costs on to working families."

records.name: Shelley Moore Capito
records.what: On efforts to bring a data center to Logan County, said 'We want them in West Virginia. They are massive investments, billions of dollars,' and 'The appetite for power is going to be so huge. Everyone's going to win here.'

records.name: Lisa Murkowski
records.what: Introduced the Department of Energy AI Act with Sen. Joe Manchin; the bill directs DOE to "study the growth of computing data centers and the electrical power load." Her quoted remarks concern AI for science and permitting, not data centers.

records.name: Roger F. Wicker
records.what: Statement on the groundbreaking of Amazon Web Services' $10 billion, two-campus hyperscale data-center project in Madison County, calling it "a historic investment in our state" and pledging to keep Mississippi attractive to business.

records.name: John Hoeven
records.what: Letter read at Applied Digital's Ellendale data-center energizing ceremony saying "technology is serving as the third wave of our state's economic growth following expansion in agriculture and energy" and that the facility provides infrastructure and computing capacity across industries.

records.name: Kevin Cramer
records.what: Letter read by his constituent-services representative at Applied Digital's Ellendale data-center energizing ceremony, saying that with North Dakota's "wide open spaces, abundant energy and ideal climate, there is a bright future for additional development within our state."

records.name: Steve Daines
records.what: Announced at his Montana 'On the Rise' Economic Summit a Bitzero investment to build a 50 MW data center powered by Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes hydropower, saying it would "support good-paying jobs in Montana" and keep the state "at the forefront of the energy and technology sector."

records.name: Mike Crapo
records.what: Statement in the Idaho Commerce announcement of Meta's $800 million Kuna data center: 'This is a promising step for job growth and opportunities in the community,' noting the center is expected to be supported by renewable energy.
records.source_name: Idaho Department of Commerce press release

records.name: James E. Risch
records.what: Statement in the Idaho Commerce announcement of Meta's Kuna data center: 'The creation of new jobs is of utmost importance in a community growing as rapidly as the Treasure Valley,' saying the center 'will provide hardworking Idahoans with good-paying jobs.'
records.source_name: Idaho Department of Commerce press release

records.name: Susan M. Collins
records.what: Joined Sen. King at the Millinocket celebration welcoming Nautilus Data Technologies' water-cooled, hydro-powered data center to the former Great Northern Paper mill site, calling it "one of the greenest facilities in the world."

records.name: Angus S. King, Jr.
records.what: Joined Sen. Collins at the Millinocket celebration welcoming Nautilus Data Technologies' water-cooled, 100% hydro-powered data center to the former Great Northern Paper mill site, saying "sustainable projects like this are the blueprint for Maine's future" and "create good jobs that strengthen our communities."

records.name: John Hoeven
records.what: Spoke at the groundbreaking of Midco's $12 million Tier III data center in Fargo, calling fast, secure data services vital across energy, health care, and other sectors and the facility important infrastructure for attracting national companies.

records.name: Tammy Duckworth
records.what: Cosponsored the Power for the People Act, making data-center operators pay the grid costs they create.
records.source_name: Sen. Welch joins bill so Americans aren't footing big data-center costs (2026)
